claim: The PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) pathway controls transposon expression in animal germ cells, thereby ensuring genome stability over generations.
source: The PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) pathway controls transposon expression in animal germ cells, thereby ensuring genome stability over generations.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the piRNA pathway's function, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: In Drosophila, piRNAs are intergenerationally inherited through the maternal lineage.
source: In Drosophila, piRNAs are intergenerationally inherited through the maternal lineage, and this has demonstrated importance in the specification of piRNA source loci and in silencing of I- and P-elements in the germ cells of daughters.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and established knowledge in the field.

claim: Maternally inherited piRNAs have demonstrated importance in the specification of piRNA source loci and in silencing of I- and P-elements in the germ cells of daughters.
source: In Drosophila, piRNAs are intergenerationally inherited through the maternal lineage, and this has demonstrated importance in the specification of piRNA source loci and in silencing of I- and P-elements in the germ cells of daughters.
evidence: This is supported by prior research cited in the manuscript.

claim: Maternally inherited Piwi protein enters somatic nuclei in early embryos prior to zygotic genome activation.
source: Maternally inherited Piwi protein enters somatic nuclei in early embryos prior to zygotic genome activation and persists therein for roughly half of the time required to complete embryonic development.
evidence: This is a direct observation reported in the manuscript, supported by experimental data.

claim: Maternally inherited Piwi protein persists in somatic nuclei for roughly half of the time required to complete embryonic development.
source: Maternally inherited Piwi protein enters somatic nuclei in early embryos prior to zygotic genome activation and persists therein for roughly half of the time required to complete embryonic development.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in the study.

claim: Maternally deposited Piwi can be cleared from newly laid embryos within 30 min using a conditionally unstable Piwi protein.
source: This enabled maternally deposited Piwi to be cleared from newly laid embryos within 30 min and well ahead of the activation of zygotic transcription.
evidence: This is a direct experimental result from the study using the AID system.

claim: Maternally deposited Piwi attenuates zygotic transposon expression in somatic cells of the developing embryo.
source: Examination of RNA and protein profiles over time, and correlation with patterns of H3K9me3 deposition, suggests a role for maternally deposited Piwi in attenuating zygotic transposon expression in somatic cells of the developing embryo.
evidence: This is inferred from RNA-seq, protein analysis, and ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Robust deposition of piRNAs targeting roo results in the deposition of transient heterochromatic marks at active roo insertions.
source: In particular, robust deposition of piRNAs targeting roo, an element whose expression is mainly restricted to embryonic development, results in the deposition of transient heterochromatic marks at active roo insertions.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing H3K9me3 marks at roo insertions and small RNA-seq data showing piRNAs targeting roo.

claim: roo expression is mainly restricted to embryonic development.
source: In particular, robust deposition of piRNAs targeting roo, an element whose expression is mainly restricted to embryonic development, results in the deposition of transient heterochromatic marks at active roo insertions.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing high roo expression during embryogenesis and low expression in other stages.

claim: roo may have adopted a lifestyle of expression in the embryonic soma to evade silencing in germ cells.
source: We hypothesize that roo, an extremely successful mobile element, may have adopted a lifestyle of expression in the embryonic soma to evade silencing in germ cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their observations.

claim: Many transposable elements have evolved mechanisms that promote their activity specifically in gonads.
source: Many TEs have evolved mechanisms that promote their activity specifically in gonads, thereby introducing new insertions that are inherited by future generations (Kim et al., 1994; Leblanc et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Accumulation of insertional mutations in germ cells can lead to decreased population fitness and increased risk of disease.
source: Accumulation of insertional mutations in germ cells can lead to decreased population fitness and increased risk of disease (Hancks and Kazazian, 2016; Payer and Burns, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In animal gonads, the main transposon defense mechanism is the PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) pathway.
source: In animal gonads, the main transposon defense mechanism is the PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) pathway (reviewed in Czech et al., 2018; Ozata et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by review citations.

claim: The piRNA system depends on 23- to 30-nt piRNAs to distinguish transposon-derived RNAs from host-encoded transcripts.
source: At its core, this system depends on 23- to 30-nt piRNAs to distinguish transposon-derived RNAs from host-encoded transcripts and to direct their associated PIWI proteins to active TE targets.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the piRNA pathway mechanism.

claim: In Drosophila, PIWI-guided repression involves cytoplasmic post-transcriptional mRNA cleavage by Aubergine (Aub) and Argonaute-3 (Ago3).
source: In Drosophila, PIWI-guided repression involves cytoplasmic post-transcriptional mRNA cleavage by Aubergine (Aub) and Argonaute-3 (Ago3) and nuclear P-element-induced wimpy testis (Piwi) that engages nascent transposon transcripts and instructs co-transcriptional gene silencing (coTGS) through heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Drosophila piRNA pathway.

claim: Nuclear Piwi engages nascent transposon transcripts and instructs co-transcriptional gene silencing (coTGS) through heterochromatin formation.
source: In Drosophila, PIWI-guided repression involves cytoplasmic post-transcriptional mRNA cleavage by Aubergine (Aub) and Argonaute-3 (Ago3) and nuclear P-element-induced wimpy testis (Piwi) that engages nascent transposon transcripts and instructs co-transcriptional gene silencing (coTGS) through heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Drosophila piRNA pathway.

claim: coTGS requires additional factors acting downstream of Piwi, including Panoramix (Panx), Nuclear Export Factor 2 (Nxf2), NTF2-related export protein 1 (Nxt1), and Cut-up (Ctp), that together form the PICTS complex (also known as SFiNX).
source: coTGS requires additional factors acting downstream of Piwi, including Panoramix (Panx), Nuclear Export Factor 2 (Nxf2), NTF2-related export protein 1 (Nxt1), and Cut-up (Ctp), that together form the PICTS complex (also known as SFiNX) (Batki et al., 2019; Eastwood et al., 2021; Fabry et al., 2019; Murano et al., 2019; Schnabl et al., 2021; Sienski et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: PICTS interfaces with general chromatin silencing factors including Su(var)205/HP1a, SETDB1/Eggless (Egg), and its co-factor Windei (Wde), Su(var)3–3/Lsd1, and its co-factor coRest, Mi-2, Rpd3, Ovaries absent, and Su(var)2–10.
source: PICTS interfaces with general chromatin silencing factors including Su(var)205/HP1a, SETDB1/Eggless (Egg), and its co-factor Windei (Wde), Su(var)3–3/Lsd1, and its co-factor coRest, Mi-2, Rpd3, Ovaries absent, and Su(var)2–10 (Czech et al., 2013; Handler et al., 2013; Koch et al., 2009; Muerdter et al., 2013; Mugat et al., 2020; Ninova et al., 2020; Osumi et al., 2019; Rangan et al., 2011; Sienski et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2019; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Loci targeted by Piwi are decorated in repressive chromatin marks including trimethylated H3K9 (H3K9me3).
source: While the detailed mechanisms of transcriptional silencing remain to be established, loci targeted by Piwi are decorated in repressive chromatin marks including trimethylated H3K9 (H3K9me3) (Klenov et al., 2014; Le Thomas et al., 2013; Rozhkov et al., 2013; Sienski et al., 2012; Wang and Elgin, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Loss of Piwi in Drosophila ovaries results in de-repression of TEs and correlates with a severe reduction in H3K9me3 deposition at their corresponding genomic loci.
source: Loss of Piwi in Drosophila ovaries results in de-repression of TEs and correlates with a severe reduction in H3K9me3 deposition at their corresponding genomic loci.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research.

claim: Piwi and Aub, and to a lesser degree Ago3, have been detected as maternally deposited proteins in Drosophila embryos.
source: Piwi and Aub, and to a lesser degree Ago3, have been detected as maternally deposited proteins in Drosophila embryos (Brennecke et al., 2007; Brennecke et al., 2008; Gunawardane et al., 2007; Mani et al., 2014; Megosh et al., 2006; Rouget et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Maternally inherited PIWI proteins have been observed in the pole plasm of syncytial embryos and in pole cells, the germ cell progenitors, after cellularization.
source: Consistent with their adult roles, maternally inherited PIWI proteins have been observed in the pole plasm of syncytial embryos and in pole cells, the germ cell progenitors, after cellularization (Brennecke et al., 2008; Dufourt et al., 2017; Mani et al., 2014; Megosh et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: During the early phases of embryogenesis Piwi is also present in somatic nuclei.
source: Though, in adult flies, the piRNA pathway is restricted to the gonad, during the early phases of embryogenesis Piwi is also present in somatic nuclei (Brennecke et al., 2008; Mani et al., 2014; Megosh et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Disrupting Piwi or other piRNA pathway factors in the female parent via mutation or RNAi leads to oogenesis defects and often results in sterility or patterning defects.
source: However, probing piRNA pathway function during early embryogenesis has been hampered by a lack of suitable experimental approaches. Disrupting Piwi or other piRNA pathway factors in the female parent either via mutation or RNAi leads to oogenesis defects and often results in sterility or patterning defects that would confound the outcome of analyses (Cox et al., 1998; Czech et al., 2013; Handler et al., 2013; Khurana et al., 2010; Klattenhoff et al., 2007; Klenov et al., 2011; Li et al., 2009a; Malone et al., 2009; Mani et al., 2014; Muerdter et al., 2013; Pane et al., 2007; Park et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Transposon expression steadily increased following ZGA and peaked between 4 and 6 hr AEL.
source: TE expression steadily increased following ZGA and peaked between 4 and 6 hr AEL (Figure 1B), similar to what was noted in prior reports (Batut et al., 2013).
evidence: This is directly observed in the RNA-seq data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: At the peak, transposon RNAs correspond to ~1.7% of the total embryonic transcriptome.
source: At the peak, transposon RNAs correspond to ~1.7% of the total embryonic transcriptome, with levels at the later studied time points decreasing to below 1% of the overall transcriptome.
evidence: This is calculated from the RNA-seq data.

claim: The majority of transposon expression could be attributed to one single transposon family, roo.
source: Interestingly, the majority of transposon expression could be attributed to one single transposon family, roo (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the RNA-seq data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: At its peak at 4–6 hr AEL, reads derived from the roo TE accounted for more than 1% of the entire embryonic transcriptome.
source: At its peak at 4–6 hr AEL, reads derived from the roo TE accounted for more than 1% of the entire embryonic transcriptome, corresponding to more than 70% of all TE-derived reads overall.
evidence: This is calculated from the RNA-seq data.

claim: Reads derived from the roo TE at 4–6 hr AEL corresponded to more than 70% of all TE-derived reads overall.
source: At its peak at 4–6 hr AEL, reads derived from the roo TE accounted for more than 1% of the entire embryonic transcriptome, corresponding to more than 70% of all TE-derived reads overall.
evidence: This is calculated from the RNA-seq data.

claim: roo transcripts were detected as early as stage 6 (in gastrulating embryos ~3 hr AEL) and localized predominantly to yolk cell nuclei.
source: In agreement with our RNA-seq data, roo transcripts were detected as early as stage 6 (in gastrulating embryos ~3 hr AEL) and localized predominantly to yolk cell nuclei (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is directly observed by RNA-FISH in Figure 1D.

claim: Stage 11 embryos (~5 hr AEL) showed strong roo RNA signal in somatic cells of the mesoderm.
source: Stage 11 embryos (~5 hr AEL) showed strong roo RNA signal in somatic cells of the mesoderm, similar to earlier reports (Brönner et al., 1995; Ding and Lipshitz, 1994).
evidence: This is directly observed by RNA-FISH and supported by citations.

claim: roo transcript levels were undetectable by FISH in late-stage embryos (>10 hr AEL).
source: In contrast, roo transcript levels were undetectable by FISH in late-stage embryos (>10 hr AEL).
evidence: This is directly observed by RNA-FISH.

claim: roo is an LTR retrotransposon.
source: roo is an LTR retrotransposon and, as has been proposed for gypsy in ovarian follicle cells (Kim et al., 1994; Leblanc et al., 2000; Song et al., 1997), could potentially be packaged into virion-like particles, possibly enabling infection of germ cell precursors as a propagation mechanism.
evidence: This is established knowledge about roo.

claim: In transcriptionally silent embryos (0–2 hr AEL), over 6400 unique proteins were detected.
source: In transcriptionally silent embryos (0–2 hr AEL), we detected over 6400 unique proteins.
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: Compared to 0–2 hr embryos, the signal intensity of ~17% or 1114 proteins significantly increased (p<0.01) by over 25% in 5–7 hr AEL embryos.
source: Compared to 0–2 hr embryos, the signal intensity of ~17% or 1114 proteins significantly increased (p<0.01) by over 25% in 5–7 hr AEL embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: 490 (or ~8% of) proteins significantly decreased (p<0.01) by over 25% in 5–7 hr AEL embryos compared to 0–2 hr embryos.
source: We also detected 490 (or ~8% of) proteins that significantly decreased (p<0.01) by over 25% in 5–7 hr AEL embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: The majority of proteins (4652 or 72%) did not change by more than 25% between 0–2 hr and 5–7 hr AEL embryos.
source: The majority of proteins (4652 or 72%), however, did not change by more than 25% between 0–2 hr and 5–7 hr AEL embryos.
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: Compared to the early time point (0–2 hr AEL), 5–7 hr AEL embryos showed significant accumulation of roo peptides (p<0.01).
source: Compared to the early time point (0–2 hr AEL), 5–7 hr AEL embryos showed significant accumulation of roo peptides (p<0.01) corresponding to its expression peak.
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: roo encodes a single ORF (with a predicted protein weight of 272 kDa), which contains a group-specific antigen-like protein (gag), a reverse transcriptase (RT/pol), an envelope protein (env), two peptidases-like domains (Pep), and a zinc finger.
source: roo encodes a single ORF (with a predicted protein weight of 272 kDa), which contains a group-specific antigen-like protein (gag), a reverse transcriptase (RT/pol), an envelope protein (env), two peptidases-like domains (Pep), and a zinc finger (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and protein domain prediction.

claim: Peptides corresponding to the gag, pol, and env proteins of roo were detected.
source: We detected peptides corresponding to the gag, pol, and env proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, bottom), indicating potential competence for retrotransposition.
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: Detection of gag, pol, and env peptides from roo indicates potential competence for retrotransposition.
source: We detected peptides corresponding to the gag, pol, and env proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, bottom), indicating potential competence for retrotransposition.
evidence: This is inferred from the detection of these specific peptides.

claim: roo ORFs remained detectable at 10–12 hr AEL.
source: Of note, roo ORFs remained detectable at 10–12 hr AEL (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F), possibly suggesting substantial stability, as this was a time at which roo mRNA levels had diminished.
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: With the exception of Piwi, genes involved in coTGS were both maternally deposited and zygotically expressed during the first ~10 hr of embryogenesis.
source: With the exception of Piwi, genes involved in coTGS were both maternally deposited and zygotically expressed during the first ~10 hr of embryogenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is observed in the RNA-seq and proteomic data.

claim: Components of the PICTS complex, comprising Panx, Nxf2, Nxt1, and Ctp, showed abundant protein expression in the 5–7 hr and 10–12 hr AEL time intervals.
source: Components of the PICTS complex, comprising Panx, Nxf2, Nxt1, and Ctp, showed abundant protein expression in the 5–7 hr and 10–12 hr AEL time intervals.
evidence: This is directly measured by quantitative mass spectrometry.

claim: Piwi mRNA appears to be primarily maternally deposited, with zygotic transcript levels remaining low throughout embryogenesis.
source: Of note, Piwi mRNA appears to be primarily maternally deposited, with zygotic transcript levels remaining low throughout embryogenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This is observed in the RNA-seq data.

claim: Pre-blastoderm stage embryos (0.5 hr AEL) showed GFP-Piwi localized to the posterior pole where it formed a crescent-like structure.
source: As previously reported (Brennecke et al., 2008; Mani et al., 2014; Megosh et al., 2006) and consistent with its maternal deposition, we detected GFP-Piwi during the pre-blastoderm stage (NC1–9, ~0–30 min AEL) localized to the posterior pole where it formed a crescent-like structure (Video 1, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy.

claim: As embryogenesis progressed and somatic nuclei migrated to the surface (NC 9–14, ~1.5–3 hr AEL), Piwi localized to somatic nuclei and to the pole plasm surrounding the nuclei of germline progenitor cells.
source: As embryogenesis progressed and somatic nuclei migrated to the surface (NC 9–14, ~1.5–3 hr AEL), Piwi localized to somatic nuclei and to the pole plasm surrounding the nuclei of germline progenitor cells, as we and others reported earlier based on immunofluorescence staining of fixed embryos (Brennecke et al., 2008; Mani et al., 2014; Megosh et al., 2006).
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and supported by citations.

claim: Nuclear Piwi signal strongly decreased during mitotic cycles, with little fluorescence signal overlapping with H2Av-RFP during nuclear divisions.
source: In agreement with an earlier report (Mani et al., 2014), our dynamic data revealed that nuclear Piwi signal strongly decreased during mitotic cycles, with little fluorescence signal overlapping with H2Av-RFP during nuclear divisions (Video 1, Figure 2D).
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Piwi was detected in somatic nuclei throughout the first 10 hr of embryogenesis; however, signal intensity decreased over time.
source: We continued to detect Piwi expression in somatic nuclei throughout the first 10 hr of embryogenesis; however, signal intensity decreased over time.
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Similar to Piwi, both Nxf2 and Panx were detected in somatic and pole cell nuclei from the syncytial blastoderm stage.
source: Similar to Piwi, both Nxf2 and Panx were detected in somatic and pole cell nuclei from the syncytial blastoderm stage (Videos 2 and 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy.

claim: In contrast to Piwi, Panx and Nxf2 showed strong co-localization with H2Av-RFP during mitotic cycles.
source: In contrast to Piwi, Panx and Nxf2 showed strong co-localization with H2Av-RFP during mitotic cycles (Videos 2 and 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G), suggesting that while Piwi is predominantly excluded, Nxf2 and Panx are retained in the nucleoplasm during mitosis.
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy.

claim: While Piwi is predominantly excluded from nuclei during mitosis, Nxf2 and Panx are retained in the nucleoplasm during mitosis.
source: In contrast to Piwi, Panx and Nxf2 showed strong co-localization with H2Av-RFP during mitotic cycles (Videos 2 and 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G), suggesting that while Piwi is predominantly excluded, Nxf2 and Panx are retained in the nucleoplasm during mitosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-localization data.

claim: Embryos derived from females expressing GFP-Piwi showed strong maternal deposition of Piwi during early embryogenesis.
source: Embryos derived from females expressing GFP-Piwi showed strong maternal deposition of Piwi during early embryogenesis (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), with GFP fluorescence in later stage (>12 hr AEL) embryos restricted to the germline cells.
evidence: This is directly observed by immunofluorescence.

claim: Embryos derived from the reciprocal cross (control males x GFP-Piwi females) showed no GFP signal in the early embryos.
source: Consistent with maternal deposition of Piwi, embryos derived from the reciprocal cross showed no GFP signal in the early embryos (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1M).
evidence: This is directly observed by immunofluorescence.

claim: Zygotically transcribed Piwi is likely not relevant for coTGS until later in development.
source: Strikingly, Piwi of zygotic origin localized exclusively to the cytoplasm of the germ cell progenitors and was not detected in nuclei, suggesting that zygotically transcribed Piwi is likely not relevant for coTGS until later in development.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that zygotic Piwi is cytoplasmic.

claim: Piwi in both embryos and ovaries existed in complex with 23- to 28-nt piRNAs and showed nearly indistinguishable size profiles that were biased for antisense reads.
source: Piwi in both tissues existed in complex with 23- to 28-nt piRNAs and showed nearly indistinguishable size profiles that were biased for antisense reads (Figure 2—figure supplement 1N, O).
evidence: This is directly measured by small RNA-seq.

claim: Piwi in ovaries showed higher levels of antisense piRNAs targeting the TEs mdg1 and 412.
source: Piwi in ovaries showed higher levels of antisense piRNAs targeting the TEs mdg1 and 412, in agreement with the majority of these small RNAs originating from the soma-specific flam piRNA cluster (Brennecke et al., 2007; Malone et al., 2009; Zanni et al., 2013).
evidence: This is directly measured by small RNA-seq and supported by citations.

claim: Piwi in embryos showed high levels of antisense piRNAs targeting roo (~16% or all TE-targeting reads) and 297 (~9%).
source: Piwi in embryos showed high levels of antisense piRNAs targeting roo (~16% or all TE-targeting reads) and 297 (~9%), consistent with an ability of maternally deposited Piwi to potentially recognize these TEs when expressed in the embryo.
evidence: This is directly measured by small RNA-seq.

claim: Early embryos (0–2 hr AEL) showed low levels of H3K9me3 signal at 117 euchromatic, w1118-specific roo insertions.
source: Early embryos (0–2 hr AEL) showed low levels of H3K9me3 signal at 117 euchromatic, w1118-specific roo insertions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: As development progressed, H3K9me3 levels at roo insertions increased with a peak at 6–10 hr AEL.
source: However, as development progressed, H3K9me3 levels increased with a peak at 6–10 hr AEL (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: Deposition of repressive chromatin marks correlated with the RNA expression of roo, yet the maximum of H3K9me3 accumulation lagged behind the RNA expression peak by approximately 2 hr.
source: Thus, deposition of repressive chromatin marks correlated with the RNA expression of roo, yet the maximum of H3K9me3 accumulation lagged behind the RNA expression peak by approximately 2 hr.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: The deposition of repressive marks trailed the direction of transcription and showed higher signal enrichments in the regions downstream of the transposon insertions.
source: Of note, the deposition of repressive marks trailed the direction of transcription and showed higher signal enrichments in the regions downstream of the transposon insertions, as previously observed for piRNA-dependent silencing in cell culture systems (Fabry et al., 2019; Sienski et al., 2015; Sienski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is directly observed in ChIP-seq data and supported by citations.

claim: H3K9me3 signal at euchromatic roo insertions of 16–18 hr AEL embryos showed diminished intensities compared to earlier time intervals.
source: Interestingly, H3K9me3 signal at euchromatic roo insertions of 16–18 hr AEL embryos, which lacked maternal Piwi in somatic nuclei and no longer express roo, showed diminished intensities compared to earlier time intervals.
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: Heads and ovaries showed no enrichment of H3K9me3 at euchromatic roo insertions, despite the presence of a functional piRNA pathway in ovaries.
source: Similarly, heads and ovaries, both tissues from adult flies, showed no enrichment of H3K9me3 at euchromatic roo insertions, despite the presence of a functional piRNA pathway in ovaries.
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: Maternal piRNAs program a response to a burst of roo expression during embryonic development but the deposition of H3K9me3 marks no longer occurs at developmental time points and in tissues where roo is not expressed.
source: Considered together, these data suggest that maternal piRNAs program a response to a burst of roo expression during embryonic development but that the deposition of H3K9me3 marks, likely directed via coTGS, no longer occurs at developmental time points and in tissues where roo is not expressed.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Genomic loci in close proximity to euchromatic, w1118-specific 297 insertions (n = 20) showed dynamic deposition of H3K9me3 similar to roo.
source: Genomic loci in close proximity to euchromatic, w1118-specific 297 insertions (n = 20) showed dynamic deposition of H3K9me3 similar to roo (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: While H3K9me3 levels at roo insertions peaked between 6 and 10 hr AEL, 297 insertions showed the maximum H3K9me3 signal intensity between 2 and 8 hr AEL.
source: However, while H3K9me3 levels at roo insertions peaked between 6 and 10 hr AEL, 297 insertions showed the maximum H3K9me3 signal intensity between 2 and 8 hr AEL, suggesting that these loci are targeted by coTGS earlier than roo insertions.
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: H3K9me3 occupancy at transposons such as mdg1 and 412 that were expressed during embryogenesis but lacked substantial maternal deposition of piRNAs retained low H3K9me3 levels throughout embryogenesis.
source: In contrast, H3K9me3 occupancy at transposons such as mdg1 and 412 that were expressed during embryogenesis but lacked substantial maternal deposition of piRNAs retained low H3K9me3 levels throughout embryogenesis, though they showed a strong enrichment in ovaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: H3K9me3 signal at constitutive heterochromatin remained stable throughout the sampled time points.
source: H3K9me3 signal at constitutive heterochromatin remained stable throughout the sampled time points (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), while H3K9me3 levels on chromosome 4 increased steadily throughout development (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: H3K9me3 levels on chromosome 4 increased steadily throughout development.
source: H3K9me3 signal at constitutive heterochromatin remained stable throughout the sampled time points (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), while H3K9me3 levels on chromosome 4 increased steadily throughout development (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: Feeding flies for 24 hr with 5 mM auxin-containing yeast paste was sufficient to induce complete degradation of Piwi in ovaries.
source: Feeding flies for 24 hr with 5 mM auxin-containing yeast paste was sufficient to induce complete degradation of Piwi in ovaries (Figure 4B, C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and this depletion resulted in the de-repression of transposons (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is directly measured by western blot and immunofluorescence.

claim: Piwi depletion in ovaries resulted in the de-repression of transposons.
source: Feeding flies for 24 hr with 5 mM auxin-containing yeast paste was sufficient to induce complete degradation of Piwi in ovaries (Figure 4B, C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and this depletion resulted in the de-repression of transposons (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is directly measured by qRT-PCR.

claim: Following a 1-day treatment, embryos laid by Piwi-depleted females developed without defects and showed similar hatching rates as their control treated siblings.
source: Following a 1-day treatment, embryos laid by Piwi-depleted females developed without defects and showed similar hatching rates as their control treated siblings (Figure 4E, F).
evidence: This is directly observed by counting hatched embryos.

claim: Longer auxin treatments resulted in more frequent deformation of embryos that was accompanied by reduced hatching rates.
source: Longer auxin treatments resulted in more frequent deformation of embryos that was accompanied by reduced hatching rates (Figure 4E, F), likely due to patterning defects as a result of Piwi depletion from follicle cells.
evidence: This is directly observed by counting hatched embryos and observing embryo morphology.

claim: In dechorionated embryos, a near complete degradation of Piwi protein was observed following 30 min auxin treatment of embryos collected for 0–30 min AEL.
source: However, in dechorionated embryos we observed a near complete degradation of Piwi protein following 30 min auxin treatment of embryos collected for 0–30 min AEL (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is directly measured by western blot.

claim: Early blastoderm embryos treated with 5 mM auxin showed rapid degradation of GFP-AID-Piwi signal, which was undetectable after 25 min of treatment.
source: Early blastoderm embryos treated with 5 mM auxin showed rapid degradation of GFP-AID-Piwi signal, which was undetectable after 25 min of treatment (Figure 5C, Video 4).
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The removal of maternal Piwi in the early time window did not significantly affect the embryo hatching rate.
source: Of note, the removal of maternal Piwi in this time window did not significantly affect the embryo hatching rate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is directly measured by counting hatched embryos.

claim: The majority of transposons showed no significant expression change upon Piwi depletion; however, roo and 297 were significantly de-repressed (p<0.05) by more than twofold.
source: The majority of transposons showed no significant expression change upon Piwi depletion; however, roo and 297 were significantly de-repressed (p<0.05) by more than twofold (Figure 5D), suggesting that Piwi impacts their expression during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is directly measured by RNA-seq and differential expression analysis.

claim: Piwi impacts roo and 297 expression during embryogenesis.
source: The majority of transposons showed no significant expression change upon Piwi depletion; however, roo and 297 were significantly de-repressed (p<0.05) by more than twofold (Figure 5D), suggesting that Piwi impacts their expression during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the de-repression observed upon Piwi depletion.

claim: Piwi depletion severely impacted H3K9me3 signal over the transposon consensus sequence of roo and 297, but not that of other TEs.
source: Piwi depletion severely impacted H3K9me3 signal over the transposon consensus sequence of roo and 297, but not that of other TEs (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq and differential enrichment analysis.

claim: 154 bins with significantly reduced (p<0.05) H3K9me3 occupancy were identified, while only two bins showed an increase.
source: We identified 154 bins with significantly reduced (p<0.05) H3K9me3 occupancy, while only two bins showed an increase.
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq and differential enrichment analysis.

claim: Of the bins with lower H3K9me3 signal, 122 and 10 were within 5 kb of roo or 297 insertions, respectively.
source: Of the bins with lower H3K9me3 signal, 122 and 10 were within 5 kb of roo or 297 insertions, respectively, thereby illustrating the impact of Piwi on chromatin states at genomic loci specifically targeted by maternal piRNAs.
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq and differential enrichment analysis.

claim: 205 and 63 individual euchromatic, degron strain-specific TE insertions of both roo and 297, respectively, showed a strong decrease of H3K9me3 levels in Piwi-depleted embryos.
source: Furthermore, 205 and 63 individual euchromatic, degron strain-specific TE insertions of both roo and 297, respectively, showed a strong decrease of H3K9me3 levels in Piwi-depleted embryos (Figure 5F, G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–F), while H3K9me3 levels at constitutive heterochromatin and on chromosome 4 were not affected (Figure 5H, I).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: H3K9me3 levels at constitutive heterochromatin and on chromosome 4 were not affected by Piwi depletion.
source: Furthermore, 205 and 63 individual euchromatic, degron strain-specific TE insertions of both roo and 297, respectively, showed a strong decrease of H3K9me3 levels in Piwi-depleted embryos (Figure 5F, G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–F), while H3K9me3 levels at constitutive heterochromatin and on chromosome 4 were not affected (Figure 5H, I).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: While roo and 297 TE levels were elevated upon auxin treatment in 2.5–3 hr AEL embryos, transposon expression returned to baseline levels comparable to untreated embryos in 6–7 hr and 7–8 hr AEL time intervals.
source: Of note, while roo and 297 TE levels were elevated upon auxin treatment in 2.5–3 hr AEL embryos, transposon expression returned to baseline levels comparable to untreated embryos in 6–7 hr and 7–8 hr AEL time intervals (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is directly measured by qRT-PCR.

claim: The data strongly indicate a relationship between the deposition of repressive H3K9me3 chromatin marks at transposon insertions and maternally deposited Piwi-piRNA complexes.
source: Taken together, these data strongly indicate a relationship between the deposition of repressive H3K9me3 chromatin marks at transposon insertions and maternally deposited Piwi-piRNA complexes (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is inferred from the combined RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data showing effects of Piwi depletion.

claim: Maternal piRNAs are critical in the suppression of hybrid dysgenesis induced by paternal transmission of I- or P-elements in matings with females that lack these transposons.
source: Indeed, maternal piRNAs are critical in the suppression of hybrid dysgenesis induced by paternal transmission of I- or P-elements in matings with females that lack these transposons (Brennecke et al., 2008; Khurana et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Epigenetic modifications induced by piRNAs appear to aid in piRNA cluster definition in the germline.
source: Epigenetic modifications induced by piRNAs appear to aid in piRNA cluster definition in the germline (Akkouche et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Maternally deposited Aub-piRNA complexes have been implicated in embryonic gene regulation.
source: Additionally, maternally deposited Aub-piRNA complexes have been implicated in embryonic gene regulation (Barckmann et al., 2015; Dufourt et al., 2017; Rouget et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Maternally inherited piRNAs control transposon expression in interspecies hybrids between Drosophila melanogaster and Drosophila simulans.
source: Last, maternally inherited piRNAs control transposon expression in interspecies hybrids between Drosophila melanogaster and Drosophila simulans (Kelleher et al., 2012) and regulate the TE tirant in the somatic compartment of the female gonad in D. simulans (Akkouche et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Maternally inherited piRNAs regulate the TE tirant in the somatic compartment of the female gonad in D. simulans.
source: Last, maternally inherited piRNAs control transposon expression in interspecies hybrids between Drosophila melanogaster and Drosophila simulans (Kelleher et al., 2012) and regulate the TE tirant in the somatic compartment of the female gonad in D. simulans (Akkouche et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Nuclear localization of Piwi lags behind in germ cell precursor nuclei, and this correlates with the observation that these nuclei activate transcription of their genomes later in embryogenesis than somatic nuclei do.
source: Notably, nuclear translocation of Piwi lags behind in germ cell precursor nuclei, and this correlates with the observation that these nuclei activate transcription of their genomes later in embryogenesis than somatic nuclei do (Van Doren et al., 1998; Zalokar, 1976).
evidence: This is observed in the study and supported by citations.

claim: Piwi shuttles out of nuclei during mitosis.
source: Our dynamic imaging of Piwi localization also revealed that it shuttles out of nuclei during mitosis, as previously observed (Mani et al., 2014).
evidence: This is directly observed by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and supported by a citation.

claim: Nuclear localization of Piwi is conditional upon its binding to a piRNA partner.
source: Several studies have previously shown that nuclear localization of Piwi is conditional upon its binding to a piRNA partners (Klenov et al., 2011; Saito et al., 2009; Yashiro et al., 2018), but we have no indication that Piwi is unloaded and reloaded during mitotic cycles.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The evolution of the abbreviated piRNA pathway in ovarian follicle cells arose as a consequence of the lifestyle adopted by gypsy family elements.
source: It has been suggested that the evolution of the abbreviated piRNA pathway in ovarian follicle cells arose as a consequence of the lifestyle adopted by gypsy family elements.
evidence: This is a hypothesis discussed in the manuscript.

claim: gypsy family elements show their highest expression levels in the support cells surrounding the developing germline.
source: These retrotransposons show their highest expression levels in the support cells surrounding the developing germline.
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: gypsy family elements encode an envelope protein and have been shown to assemble into virus-like particles.
source: gypsy family elements encode an envelope protein and have been shown to assemble into virus-like particles (Kim et al., 1994; Leblanc et al., 2000; Song et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: roo is a quite successful element, as indicated by it being the element with the highest copy number of individual insertions in the sequenced strains.
source: While this remains speculative, it does provoke questions of whether a similar strategy is adopted by roo in the embryo. roo is a quite successful element, as indicated by it being the element with the highest copy number of individual insertions in our sequenced strains (9.4% of all identified TE insertions in the w1118 strain and 9.9% in our degron line).
evidence: This is directly measured by whole-genome sequencing.

claim: roo expression is extremely low in the ovary.
source: How this is achieved remains mysterious since roo expression is extremely low in the ovary.
evidence: This is observed in the RNA-seq data.

claim: roo does not appear to be a target of the ovarian piRNA pathway since its gonadal expression is not increased nor does its HP1a enrichment and H3K9me3 levels change in piRNA pathway mutant animals.
source: Moreover, roo does not appear to be a target of the ovarian piRNA pathway since its gonadal expression is not increased nor does its HP1a enrichment and H3K9me3 levels change in piRNA pathway mutant animals (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H, I; Senti et al., 2015; Wang and Elgin, 2011).
evidence: This is observed in the data and supported by citations.

claim: roo expression is activated by twist (twi) and snail (sna), which are highly expressed in the embryogenic mesoderm.
source: Previous studies have suggested that roo expression is activated by twist (twi) and snail (sna), which are highly expressed in the embryogenic mesoderm (Brönner et al., 1995), and this is consistent with the spatial expression pattern that we also observe.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research and consistent with observations in the study.

claim: roo expresses the full repertoire of proteins needed to form virus-like particles.
source: roo expresses the full repertoire of proteins needed to form virus-like particles, and its high expression levels (exceeding 1% of the transcriptome at its peak) might enable a strategy of propagation by infection in trans, even if rates of transmission to the germ cell precursors are relatively low.
evidence: This is observed in the proteomic data.

claim: Only maternally deposited piRNAs engage Piwi in the soma of the developing embryo.
source: Our data strongly suggests that only maternally deposited piRNAs engage Piwi in the soma of the developing embryo.
evidence: This is inferred from the reciprocal cross experiments and small RNA-seq data.

claim: 16% of maternally deposited piRNAs target roo.
source: Indeed, 16% of maternally deposited piRNAs target roo.
evidence: This is directly measured by small RNA-seq.

claim: H3K9me3 marks build at presumably active, euchromatic roo insertions as embryos progress toward stage 13 (10 hr AEL).
source: Consistent with its recognition by Piwi-piRNA complexes and recruitment of the PICTS/SFiNX complex, H3K9me3 marks build at presumably active, euchromatic roo insertions as embryos progress toward stage 13 (10 hr AEL).
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq.

claim: The peak of H3K9me3 abundance lags about 2 hr behind the peak of transcription.
source: The peak of H3K9me3 abundance lags about 2 hr behind the peak of transcription.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: By 13 hr AEL, H3K9me3 peaks over roo insertions have disappeared, but roo expression has not returned.
source: Imposition of a repressive chromatin state on roo is transient during somatic development. By 13 hr AEL, H3K9me3 peaks over roo insertions have disappeared, but roo expression has not returned.
evidence: This is directly measured by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq.

claim: The lack of H3K9me3 at late stages correlates with the absence of critical piRNA pathway proteins in the soma.
source: The lack of H3K9me3 also correlates with the absence of critical piRNA pathway proteins in the soma.
evidence: This is inferred from the proteomic and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Zygotic depletion of maternal Piwi during early embryogenesis produces a statistically significant change in roo expression (roughly twofold).
source: Though zygotic depletion of maternal Piwi during early embryogenesis does produce a statistically significant change in roo expression (roughly twofold), this transposon remains highly expressed reaching up to 1% of the entire transcriptome in control animals, despite being targeted by the piRNA pathway.
evidence: This is directly measured by RNA-seq.

claim: roo remains highly expressed reaching up to 1% of the entire transcriptome in control animals, despite being targeted by the piRNA pathway.
source: Though zygotic depletion of maternal Piwi during early embryogenesis does produce a statistically significant change in roo expression (roughly twofold), this transposon remains highly expressed reaching up to 1% of the entire transcriptome in control animals, despite being targeted by the piRNA pathway.
evidence: This is directly measured by RNA-seq.

claim: Roo is expressed in ovaries at very low levels, yet the hallmarks of piRNA-dependent silencing, specifically H3K9me3, are absent from euchromatic roo insertions.
source: Roo is expressed in ovaries at very low levels, yet the hallmarks of piRNA-dependent silencing, specifically H3K9me3, are absent from euchromatic roo insertions.
evidence: This is directly measured by RNA-seq and ChIP-seq.

claim: Ovaries produce abundant roo piRNAs, and these are overwhelmingly in the antisense orientation.
source: Nonetheless, ovaries produce abundant roo piRNAs, and these are overwhelmingly in the antisense orientation.
evidence: This is directly measured by small RNA-seq.

claim: The only uni-strand cluster expressed in germ cells, cluster 20A, has collected roo insertions in the antisense orientation.
source: Additionally, the only uni-strand cluster expressed in germ cells, cluster 20A, has collected roo insertions in the antisense orientation.
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: Recognition of a locus by the piRNA pathway does not necessarily impose the creation of a mitotically heritable epigenetic state.
source: Perhaps more importantly, our study demonstrates that recognition of a locus by the piRNA pathway does not necessarily impose the creation of a mitotically heritable epigenetic state.
evidence: This is inferred from the transient nature of H3K9me3 marks observed in the study.

claim: Heterochromatin-mediated silencing of somatic transposons requires the continuous presence of the piRNA machinery in follicle cells.
source: This is consistent with observations made by many groups in follicle cells wherein heterochromatin-mediated silencing of somatic transposons requires the continuous presence of the piRNA machinery (Batki et al., 2019; Clark et al., 2017; Dönertas et al., 2013; Fabry et al., 2019; Muerdter et al., 2013; Murano et al., 2019; Ohtani et al., 2013; Saito et al., 2009; Sienski et al., 2015; Sienski et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Loss of transposon control in the embryonic soma does not result in an overt morphological phenotype.
source: Although loss of transposon control in the embryonic soma does not result in an overt morphological phenotype, our results suggest that the piRNA pathway indeed plays a role in regulating the somatic chromatin structure during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is directly observed in the study.

claim: The piRNA pathway plays a role in regulating the somatic chromatin structure during early embryogenesis.
source: Although loss of transposon control in the embryonic soma does not result in an overt morphological phenotype, our results suggest that the piRNA pathway indeed plays a role in regulating the somatic chromatin structure during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing H3K9me3 changes upon Piwi depletion.
